data.narrative:
Walden Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company led by co-founder and CEO Russ Tedrake, an MIT professor and former SVP of Large Behavior Models at Toyota Research Institute. The company carries a current post-money valuation of $1.1B on $300M raised to date. The valuation assessment leverages a peer universe of nine same-sector, similar-valuation-tier comparables, comprising eight private companies and one public listing, including later-stage operators such as Divergent (Series E, $2.3B), Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), and Locus Robotics (Series F, $2.0B).

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression methodology applies a typical Seed-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.5x to the $1.1B base, implying $2.8B. Peer-median analysis across the nine-company comparison set yields $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B. These methods reflect differing assumptions: stage-progression assumes material de-risking, while peer-median anchors to observable market pricing of comparable robotics companies at various advancement levels.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $1.5B (low) to $3.2B (high), with a median of $2.2B. The $1.1B current valuation sits below this range, suggesting upside potential conditional on execution. Key uncertainties include the degree of product-market fit validation and the timing of next fundraising, which will clarify stage progression assumptions.
